gaps.sentence: If you mix blue and yellow, you always ___ green.
gaps.explanation: The adverb 'always' signals a timeless result, so the present simple fits: get.

gaps.sentence: If people ___ less time on their phones, they would read more.
gaps.explanation: An unreal present habit takes the past simple in the if-clause: spent.

gaps.sentence: She wishes she ___ the job offer when it came.
gaps.explanation: Regret about a past decision takes the past perfect: had accepted.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ my umbrella — I am getting soaked!
gaps.hint: present regret about an earlier decision
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus the past perfect expresses a present regret about a past decision: had brought.

gaps.sentence: If it ___ tomorrow, the match will be cancelled.
gaps.explanation: In first conditionals the if-clause takes the present simple even with future meaning: rains.

gaps.sentence: If only we ___ the tickets before they sold out!
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus the past perfect regrets a missed past opportunity: had bought.

gaps.sentence: You'd have got a better exchange rate ___ at the bank instead of the airport.
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes 'if + past perfect'.

gaps.sentence: ___ you mix blue and red, you get purple.
gaps.explanation: General truths: if + present simple, present simple.
